_about: ITU-T Y.3172 pipeline traceability (DOCX §4.3 / §7.4). Each stage quotes the
Y.3172 definition from the ingested Recommendation, names the project components
that perform it, and follows one quoted provision of a recorded run through it.
Each stage also states how it corresponds to the Y.3172 node (direct or by
analogy); Y.3172 components with no counterpart are listed separately.
standard: ITU-T Recommendation Y.3172 (06/2019) Architectural framework for machine learning in future networks including IMT-2020
compliance_disclaimer: Architectural correspondence only, mostly by analogy (see correspondence per stage). Formal Y.3172 compliance has not been assessed and is not claimed; the clause 7 requirements for ML in networks are not addressed by the current architecture.
scope_note: ITU-T Y.3172 specifies an architecture for machine learning in networks: ML pipeline nodes read data from network functions (UE, access and core network) and apply ML output to network targets, managed by an ML function orchestrator (MLFO) from a declarative ML Intent. This project is a policy and legal adviser whose pipeline processes legal and standards documents. The table maps that document pipeline to the Y.3172 node vocabulary; only preprocessing corresponds directly, the other stages correspond by analogy, and the components listed under components_not_implemented do not exist in the project.

y3172_definition.phrase_quoted: SRC (source): This node is the source of data that can be used as input to the ML pipeline.

project_implementation.description: Official source documents listed with provenance in the source manifest.
project_implementation.evidence_preserved: title evidence string, URL, SHA-256, retrieval date, provenance note

pipeline_stages.difference_from_y3172: Y.3172 SRC nodes are network data sources such as UE, SMF or AF (clause 8.1, NOTE 2); here the sources are legal and standards documents.

y3172_definition.phrase_quoted: C (collector): This node is responsible for collecting data from one or more SRC nodes.

project_implementation.description: Text extraction with page provenance (PyMuPDF; python-docx for 3GPP); a file is refused if its title evidence is absent.
project_implementation.evidence_preserved: extracted character count, page numbers, refusal on wrong file

pipeline_stages.difference_from_y3172: A Y.3172 collector may also configure its SRC nodes, e.g. via RRC or OAM (clause 8.1, NOTE 3); document extraction configures nothing.

y3172_definition.phrase_quoted: PP (preprocessor): This node is responsible for cleaning data

project_implementation.description: Running headers/footers removed, sections detected from printed headings or PDF bookmarks, chunked within one section.
project_implementation.evidence_preserved: section label, section heading, page, chunk ID

pipeline_stages.difference_from_y3172: Cleans and segments the collected data into the form the model consumes, as clause 8.1 describes for PP.

y3172_definition.phrase_quoted: M (model): This is a machine learning model, in a form which is usable in a machine learning pipeline.

project_implementation.description: Sentence-embedding model for retrieval within each agent's own KB. No generative model: agents quote retrieved passages.
project_implementation.generator_model: none — agents quote retrieved passages; no generative model is used
project_implementation.generator_model_scope: Applies to the policy adviser (src/). The separate incident-response lab (ir/llm.py) can use a Claude model through the Anthropic API (LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic); without a key or the SDK it falls back to the deterministic offline playbook.
project_implementation.evidence_preserved: query, cosine similarity, knowledge base searched

queries: Unusual authentication and signalling attempts are observed on the affected private 5G slice.
telecommunication entity reporting of a security incident and the time limit
types of cyber security incidents that must be reported to CERT-In
measures a telecommunication entity must take to protect telecom cyber security
unauthorised access attempts and attacks on network infrastructure

pipeline_stages.difference_from_y3172: The embedding model only ranks passages for retrieval; it is not trained here and makes no prediction about a network. Agent selection (src/core/orchestrator.py) uses keyword rules and claim support (src/core/verifier.py) is a lexical term-coverage check, so neither decision is made by the model.

y3172_definition.phrase_quoted: P (policy): This node enables the application of policies to the output of the model node.

project_implementation.description: The Verifier checks each claim against the Canonical KB (cited source/section exists, text supports the claim, in-force and amendment status) and assigns VERIFIED / INCOMPLETE / UNSUPPORTED / CONFLICT; cross-domain links and conflicts.
project_implementation.evidence_preserved: verifier outcome and rationale per claim

worked_trace.verifier_rationale: Supported by the authoritative text (Telecommunications (Telecom Cyber Security) Rules, 2024, Rule 7), but amendments not checked for this source. Recorded status: in force from 21 November 2024 (rule 1(2): on publication in the Official Gazette).

pipeline_stages.difference_from_y3172: The Y.3172 P node applies operator policies to model output to limit its impact before it is applied to a live network (clause 8.1, NOTE 5); here the Verifier applies evidence rules to the agents' claims, and nothing is applied to a network.

y3172_definition.phrase_quoted: D (distributor): This node is responsible for identifying the SINK(s) and distributing the output of the M node

project_implementation.description: The Coordinator places each verified claim in one of the five DOCX Table A1 categories; the assessment is written to the hash-chained audit trail and shown in the UI.
project_implementation.evidence_preserved: Coordinator category, audit entry sequence number and hash

pipeline_stages.difference_from_y3172: The Y.3172 D node identifies SINK nodes and distributes the model output to them (clause 8.1, NOTE 6); here the output goes to a human reader through the Coordinator, the audit trail and the UI. No SINK node exists.

y3172_definition.phrase_quoted: machine learning sandbox: An environment in which machine learning models can be trained, tested and their effects on the network evaluated.

project_implementation.description: NOT EXECUTED — not executed — the ITU AI for Good Sandbox is not available in this environment. The Y.3172 ML sandbox (clauses 3.2.6, 8.2) is a different thing from the ITU AI for Good Sandbox platform: a subsystem of ML pipelines and simulated ML underlay networks, managed by the MLFO, in which ML models are trained and tested before deployment. Neither is part of this project. Replay of recorded runs (src/audit/replay.py) re-tests recorded runs but is not an ML sandbox.

pipeline_stages.difference_from_y3172: No ML sandbox subsystem (clause 8.2) exists: no simulated ML underlay network is used to train or test an ML model.

components_not_implemented.y3172_role: Target of the ML output, which takes action on it (e.g. a UE adjusting its measurement periodicity).
components_not_implemented.project_status: Not implemented. The adviser's output is read by a human; nothing acts on a network.

components_not_implemented.y3172_role: Manages and orchestrates the ML pipeline nodes: selects and reselects ML models on performance, places and chains the nodes, based on the ML Intent.
components_not_implemented.project_status: Not implemented. The Swarm Orchestrator selects specialist agents with keyword rules on the released scenario text; it does not select models, place or chain pipeline nodes, or react to model performance.

components_not_implemented.y3172_role: Declarative, technology-agnostic specification of an ML application: data sources, model repositories, output targets, constraints and time constraints.
components_not_implemented.project_status: Not implemented. Scenario chunks are incident descriptions, not ML application specifications.

components_not_implemented.component: ML underlay networks and simulated ML underlay networks
components_not_implemented.y3172_role: The network whose functions provide data to, and receive output from, the ML pipeline; a simulated one feeds the ML sandbox.
components_not_implemented.project_status: Not connected. The adviser reads no network data. The incident-response lab's simulated 5G core could serve as a simulated underlay but is not connected to an ML pipeline.

components_not_implemented.y3172_role: Interfaces between the ML pipeline, sandbox and management subsystems, the underlay networks, and pipeline nodes on different levels.
components_not_implemented.project_status: Not implemented. Components call each other in one Python process.

components_not_implemented.y3172_role: Pipeline nodes instantiated at different levels (e.g. UE, AN, CN).
components_not_implemented.project_status: Not implemented. The pipeline runs in a single process; agents run sequentially.
